properties.decision:
ACCEPTED 2026-08-23 on Anthony's word. Captured the day before as brainstorming and promoted unchanged when he was asked to settle the seam question — the wording below is his, from the capture, and is preserved rather than rewritten.

THIS IS HIS ANSWER TO THE QUESTION `fact:coupling-and-contract-are-recorded-in-vocabularies-that-never-meet` DELIBERATELY LEFT TO THE OWNER: which level should carry contracts.

HIS WORDS: "say we have a subsystem_A <--> subsystem_B interface - my thoughts this should be defined at the lowest level that actually defines the interface and the rest is rolled up so that if somebody asked at a high level, 'is there an interface between subsystem_A and subsystem_B?' the 'view' capturing at subsystem to subsystem level would say 'yes', but the graph would actually show it is actually subsystem_A.component_2 <--> subsystem_B.component_5 that the interface contract is actually defined."

THE DESIGN ALREADY DOES THE FIRST HALF, AND THE MEASUREMENT THAT CALLED IT A DEFECT WAS READING IT AS ONE. `fact:the-eight-subsystems-are-groupings-not-black-boxes` (2026-08-17) recorded '0 of 8 subsystems provide an interface - EVERY interface in the design is provided by a LEAF component one level down' and read that as the tier having no contracts. UNDER THIS RULE THAT IS NOT A DEFECT, IT IS THE RULE BEING FOLLOWED. A contract belongs where it is defined; a subsystem carrying its own copy would be duplicating its child's. (Re-measured 2026-08-23: it is now 4 of 10 subsystems providing, so the tier is no longer silent either way.)

=> SO WHAT IS MISSING IS NOT CONTRACTS, IT IS THE ROLL-UP. That is already an open question of its own: `dec:idea-a-view-can-slice-by-altitude-not-only-by-aspect` records that reflow2's ten views all slice by ASPECT and none by ALTITUDE, so 'show me the top level' has no projection behind it. This rule and that one are the same need approached from opposite ends — and that one is STILL OPEN, so accepting this does not mean the roll-up view exists.

WHAT IT SETTLED, and this is the sharp part: `undeclared_seam` reports 64 of 72 module pairs uncontracted, and `fact:coupling-and-contract-are-recorded-in-vocabularies-that-never-meet` measured that the number CANNOT MOVE - couplings come from DEPENDS_ON and contracts from PROVIDES/CONSUMES and the two sets are disjoint by construction. Verified independently 2026-08-23: all 64 pairs are inside ONE crate, zero cross a crate boundary, and 44 of the 55 files in reflow2-core carry `impl DesignGraph`, so most of those 'couplings' are impl blocks of the same struct. Under this rule the question becomes not 'does this pair share a contract' but 'is this coupling covered by a contract declared at or below it' — and `seam_coverage {altitude}` answers it: 72/8/64 at module, 11/11/0 at subsystem. The gap itself was acknowledged once on this design (`decision:ack:f384097e7d8b01b0`), NOT silenced by changing a detector default.

COUNTER-ARGUMENTS, recorded beside the idea before it was settled and still live:
* A roll-up VIEW must be a pure projection - this project's standing rule is that a view is a projection and renderer fill-ins are defects. Answering 'yes, A and B interface' when the edge exists only between two leaves is a DERIVATION, and it must be derived on read, never written back as an edge between the subsystems, or the graph starts asserting contracts nobody declared. `seam_coverage` honours this: it writes nothing back.
* It does not say what to do about coupling covered by NO contract at any level. That is still the real finding, and a carelessly written roll-up could hide it. THIS IS WHY the detector was left answering at module level when the alternative was offered.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether DEPENDS_ON between two impl blocks of one struct is a dependency worth recording at all - the other half of what that fact left open, offered to him as the root fix on 2026-08-23 and not taken in that pass.
properties.name: A contract is declared at the LOWEST level that actually defines it, and higher levels answer by ROLL-UP
properties.rationale: Captured at `proposed` via the brainstorm skill, 2026-08-23, as the owner's answer to a question `fact:coupling-and-contract-are-recorded-in-vocabularies-that-never-meet` explicitly left to him. ACCEPTED the same day, on Anthony's word, when he was asked to settle the 64-uncontracted-pairs seam question and chose to promote this position rather than restate it. He was offered, and declined, defaulting the undeclared-seam detector to subsystem altitude — so this rule governs how contracts are DECLARED, and changes nothing about what the detector REPORTS.
